This message comes from Odoo, the all-in-one business management software platform.

Try today for free at Odoo.com/NPRPodcasts.
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
South Carolina Republican Senator Darlene Graham is commenting on President Trump's decision to pause sanctions against Russia.
The sanctions were named after her late brother, Senator Lindsey Graham.
It's up to him whether or not he chooses to use it.
Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia to end the war and get the gas prices down.
The president has drawn bipartisan criticism for waiving the sanctions just days before they were supposed to take effect.
Trump also announced a plan to allow the sale of Russian diesel, saying it would bring down energy prices.
The White House has again shut out CNN from the video pool of five networks that share the costs and the logistics of covering the president.
But this is the first since CNN won a court ruling a few days ago over access to the White House.
NPR's David Falkenflick says the Justice Department is appealing.
CNN and MS Now and Politico sued after President Trump ordered their journalists be barred from the White House because he thought they were too negative.
A federal judge ruled that ban was likely unconstitutional and put it on hold until trial.
The pool is a different matter.
It's made up of ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC, as well as CNN.
The networks are refusing to take CNN's turn in the rotation.
There was no major TV pool coverage at the White House Friday and will be none of Trump's time in Florida this weekend in smaller spaces where the full press cannot attend.
The Justice Department is investigating the pool networks, saying their consultation over CNN's Ms. Turn may constitute illegal antitrust behavior.
David Falkenflick, NPR News.
Multiple deaths and injuries are reported at a Canadian military base in Alberta.
As Dan Carbenchuk reports, officials in the province called a code orange response to help deal with the high number of casualties coming from the base.
Canada's Defence Minister David McGinty would not say how many people were killed, adding that he's never seen anything like this in his lifetime.
A fire is still burning at the Wainwright military base training area where military personnel train under battlefield conditions.
During the night, a stream of ambulances was seen leaving the base heading for a local hospital as well as to hospitals in Edmonton.
The code orange is a disaster response protocol called when there is a high number of patients.
The Canadian Armed Forces says the process of informing next of kin is underway and the number of casualties will not be confirmed until that process is complete.
A statement from NATO says Canada does not carry this grief alone. Many other NATO personnel also train at Wainwright.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carbenchuk in Toronto.
Hurricane Trudy is bringing heavy rain and strong winds to Mexico's southwestern and west central Pacific coast.
The National Hurricane Centre says Trudy is expected to dump eight inches of rain with isolated totals of 12 inches,
authorities warn of potentially life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
You're listening to NPR.
Do teachers feel like they matter?
A news survey finds only one in three teachers say that they do.
NPR's Yannaki Mehta has the story.
When educators feel valued, they're less likely to burn out and leave the profession.
But a quarter of teachers say they're likely to leave their jobs within a year.
Among those who felt like they matter little or not at all at school, half say they don't plan to stay in education.
All this is from a news survey from Gallup, the Mattering Institute and the Walton Family Foundation, which is a financial supporter of NPR.
Eighty-five percent of teachers reported their sense of mattering comes through working directly with students and helping them work through difficult situations.
The report says schools and families can take steps to make sure their teachers feel valued by formalizing appreciation,
like by making recognition a part of school routines.
Administrators can also have regular conversations around helping school staff grow and develop their careers.
Yannaki Mehta, NPR News.
A new environmental study finds President Trump's plan to paint the Eisenhower Executive Office Building next to the White House
would diminish the historic character and the original design of the building.
The president has suggested painting the 19th century historic landmark, calling the gray exterior, in his words, "a really bad color."
The study finds the project would cost at least $7.5 million.
It also states that the granite is not meant to be painted and that doing so would trap moisture and degrade the stone.
Trump has been looking at this as part of his efforts to remake the nation's capital.
I'm Linda Kenyon.
